title: EPA 608 Type III practice test
description: Free EPA Section 608 Type III (low-pressure appliances) practice questions. Every answer is explained and linked to the section of 40 CFR Part 82 it comes from.

questions.question: The rule on pressurizing low-pressure appliances sorts refrigerants by whether they boil at or below 85 °F. At what pressure is that boiling point taken?

options.A: 29.9 inches of mercury (standard atmospheric pressure)
options.B: 45 psia
options.C: 25 mm Hg absolute
options.D: 355 psia

questions.explanation: The rule refers to refrigerants "with boiling points at or below 85 degrees Fahrenheit at 29.9 inches of mercury (standard atmospheric pressure)." The 45 and 355 psia figures come from the pressure-class definitions, and 25 mm Hg absolute is the Table 1 level for low-pressure appliances.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A chiller uses a refrigerant with a liquid phase saturation pressure of 15 psia at 104 °F. Which technician certification type does 40 CFR 82.161 require to service it?

options.A: Type I
options.B: Type II
options.C: Type III
options.D: None, because chillers are exempt

questions.explanation: A pressure "below 45 psia at 104 °F" makes this a low-pressure appliance, and persons who service low-pressure appliances "must be certified as Type III technicians." Type II covers medium-, high- and very high-pressure appliances.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A technician will service small appliances, high-pressure rooftop units and low-pressure chillers. Which certification does 40 CFR 82.161 require for someone who works on all of these appliance types?

options.A: Type III
options.B: Universal
options.C: Type II
options.D: Type I

questions.explanation: Persons who work on all appliances described in paragraph (a)(1)(i) through (iii) "must be certified as Universal technicians." Type I, II or III alone covers only one of those appliance groups.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How is the low-pressure appliance row of Table 1 in 40 CFR 82.156 stated differently from the other rows?

options.A: It changes with charge size above 200 pounds
options.B: It applies only to recovery equipment made before November 15, 1993
options.C: It sets no required level at all
options.D: Its level is given as an absolute pressure in mm Hg rather than in inches of Hg vacuum

questions.explanation: The other rows give inches of Hg vacuum, while the table lists "Low-pressure appliance" at "25 mm Hg absolute" in both equipment columns. The row has no charge-size split and applies to equipment of either age.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An owner suspends the leak repair deadlines on a chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) by mothballing it. What must the owner's records document?

options.A: When the appliance was mothballed and when additional refrigerant was added to it
options.B: The name of the EPA official who approved the mothballing
options.C: Daily temperature readings while it is shut down
options.D: Only the date the appliance is finally retired

questions.explanation: Owners or operators who suspend deadlines by mothballing "must keep records documenting when the appliance was mothballed and when additional refrigerant was added to the appliance (or isolated component)." No EPA approval or daily readings are called for.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For a repair that is not major, with no evacuation to the atmosphere afterward, how does the requirement for a low-pressure appliance differ from the one for a high-pressure appliance?

options.A: The low-pressure appliance must be evacuated to 25 mm Hg absolute instead
options.B: The low-pressure appliance has no pressure requirement
options.C: The low-pressure appliance is pressurized to no higher than 0 psig, while the high-pressure appliance is evacuated to no higher than 0 psig
options.D: The low-pressure appliance is pressurized to 5 psig

questions.explanation: A medium-, high- or very high-pressure appliance must "Be evacuated to a pressure no higher than 0 psig," while a low-pressure appliance must "Be pressurized to a pressure no higher than 0 psig before it is opened." Both share the same 0 psig ceiling, reached from opposite directions.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A low-pressure appliance uses a refrigerant that boils at or below 85 °F at 29.9 inches of mercury. It needs a repair that is not major (and not an oil change), and it will not be evacuated to the atmosphere afterward. When pressurizing it before it is opened, what does the rule prohibit?

options.A: Using heat to raise the internal pressure
options.B: Using methods such as nitrogen that require subsequent purging
options.C: Covering openings when isolation is not possible
options.D: Raising the internal pressure to 0 psig

questions.explanation: For these refrigerants, persons "must not use methods such as nitrogen that require subsequent purging." The rule does not forbid heat, it requires covering openings when isolation is not possible, and 0 psig is the required pressure limit, not a prohibited one.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A low-pressure appliance uses a refrigerant that boils above 85 °F at 29.9 inches of mercury. After heat has raised its internal pressure as much as possible, up to what pressure may nitrogen be used before the appliance is opened for a non-major repair?

options.A: 5 psig
options.B: 10 psig
options.C: 25 psig
options.D: Atmospheric pressure

questions.explanation: For these refrigerants, persons must use heat first, "but may use nitrogen to raise the internal pressure of the appliance from the level attainable through use of heat to atmospheric pressure." Nitrogen may not push the pressure above atmospheric.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A low-pressure appliance It needs a repair that is not major (and not an oil change), and it will not be evacuated to the atmosphere afterward. While pressurizing it, the technician finds that the part cannot be isolated. What does the rule require?

options.A: Cover openings
options.B: Add nitrogen to 5 psig
options.C: Notify EPA within 30 days
options.D: Replace the system receiver

questions.explanation: In the paragraph on pressurizing low-pressure appliances, the rule states: "Persons must cover openings when isolation is not possible." Nothing in that paragraph calls for adding nitrogen to 5 psig, notifying EPA, or replacing a receiver.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The oil-change provision lets oil be drained into a system receiver. How does the rule define a system receiver?

options.A: A recovery cylinder outside the appliance
options.B: A purge unit mounted on a chiller
options.C: The isolated portion of the appliance, or a specific vessel within it, used to hold the refrigerant charge during servicing or repair
options.D: A container for used oil sent to a reclaimer

questions.explanation: System receiver means "the isolated portion of the appliance, or a specific vessel within the appliance, that is used to hold the refrigerant charge during the servicing or repair of that appliance." It is part of the appliance, not an external cylinder or oil container.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: No exemption applies. Under 40 CFR 82.156(a), what kind of machine must a technician use to evacuate a low-pressure appliance to the Table 1 level?

options.A: Any vacuum pump
options.B: A recovery and/or recycling machine certified under 40 CFR 82.158
options.C: The chiller's own purge unit
options.D: Any machine approved by the chiller manufacturer

questions.explanation: Technicians must evacuate to the Table 1 levels "using a recovery and/or recycling machine certified pursuant to § 82.158." A plain vacuum pump, purge unit or manufacturer approval does not meet that requirement.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Leaks in a chiller make the Table 1 level unattainable. What is the first step 40 CFR 82.156(a)(2) lists for the person opening or disposing of it?

options.A: Add nitrogen to the leaking components
options.B: Evacuate the whole chiller to 0 psig only
options.C: Notify EPA before opening the chiller
options.D: Isolate leaking from non-leaking components wherever possible

questions.explanation: The first step is: "Isolate leaking from non-leaking components wherever possible." Non-leaking components then go to the Table 1 levels, and leaking ones to the lowest level attainable without substantially contaminating the refrigerant.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the evacuation rule, who must verify that the required evacuation level has been reached, and when?

options.A: The technician, before the appliance or part is opened
options.B: The owner, within 30 days after the repair
options.C: EPA, during an inspection
options.D: The recovery equipment manufacturer, when the machine is certified

questions.explanation: The rule says "A technician must verify that the applicable level of evacuation has been reached" in the appliance or part before it is opened. The duty falls on the technician at the time of the job, not on the owner, EPA, or the equipment maker.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The table of maximum contaminant levels for equipment advertised as recycling equipment has a column for low-pressure (R-11, R-123, R-113) systems. Which contaminant is listed as not applicable (N/A) for those systems?

options.A: Noncondensable gas
options.B: Moisture
options.C: Acid content
options.D: Particulates

questions.explanation: The "MAXIMUM LEVELS OF CONTAMINANTS PERMISSIBLE IN REFRIGERANT PROCESSED" table shows N/A for noncondensable gas in the "Low-pressure (R-11, R-123, R-113)" column, with 2.0% for the other columns. Moisture, acid content and particulates all have listed limits for low-pressure systems.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.158, Standards for recovery and/or recycling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An ice rink is cooled by a low-pressure chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant. Which category in the definitions does the ice rink appliance belong to for leak repair purposes?

options.A: Commercial refrigeration
options.B: Industrial process refrigeration
options.C: Comfort cooling
options.D: Small appliance

questions.explanation: The industrial process refrigeration definition states: "This sector also includes industrial ice machines, appliances used directly in the generation of electricity, and ice rinks." Commercial refrigeration covers retail food and cold storage, and comfort cooling covers occupied buildings.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the rolling average method in the leak rate definition, step 1 adds up the refrigerant added to the appliance over what period?

options.A: The last 30 days
options.B: The time since the appliance was installed
options.C: The current calendar month
options.D: The previous 365-day period, or the shorter period since the last successful follow-up verification test showing all identified leaks were repaired

questions.explanation: Step 1 takes "the sum of the pounds of refrigerant added to the appliance over the previous 365-day period (or over the period that has passed since the last successful follow-up verification test showing all identified leaks in the appliance were repaired, if that period is less than one year)." The sum is then divided by the full charge and multiplied by 100.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: As of April 10, 2020, which of these low-pressure chillers is covered by the federal leak repair rule in 40 CFR 82.157?

options.A: A chiller with a full charge of 60 pounds of a class II refrigerant
options.B: A chiller with a full charge of 40 pounds of a class II refrigerant
options.C: A chiller with a full charge of 300 pounds of a substitute refrigerant only
options.D: A chiller with a full charge of 45 pounds of a class I refrigerant

questions.explanation: Since April 10, 2020, the section applies only to appliances with "a full charge of 50 or more pounds" of a class I or class II refrigerant or a blend containing one. It does not apply to appliances containing solely substitute refrigerants, and the 40- and 45-pound chillers are under 50 pounds.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A chiller owner (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) asks EPA for more than 30 days to finish leak repairs. Which item must the extension request include?

options.A: A letter of support from the chiller manufacturer
options.B: Copies of the technicians' certification cards
options.C: The reasons why more than 30 days are needed to complete the repair
options.D: A photograph of each leak

questions.explanation: Extension requests must include, among other items, "the reasons why more than 30 days (or 120 days if an industrial process shutdown is required) are needed to complete the repair." Manufacturer letters, certification cards and photographs are not on the list.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: On an appliance covered by the leak repair rule (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant), a repair passed its initial verification test without the appliance being evacuated. When must the follow-up verification test be done?

options.A: Within 30 days of the initial test
options.B: Within one year of the repair
options.C: Within 60 days of the initial test
options.D: Within 10 days of the successful initial test

questions.explanation: A follow-up verification test must be performed "within 10 days of the successful initial verification test." If the appliance was evacuated, the 10 days instead run from when it reaches normal operating characteristics and conditions.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: On an appliance covered by the leak repair rule (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant), a leak repair required evacuating part of the appliance. When must the initial verification test be performed?

options.A: Before adding any refrigerant to the appliance
options.B: Only after the appliance returns to normal operating conditions
options.C: Within 10 days after the appliance is recharged
options.D: One year after the repair

questions.explanation: For repairs that require evacuation, "the test must be performed before adding any refrigerant to the appliance." Testing after the appliance returns to normal operation is the follow-up verification test, not the initial one.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A comfort cooling chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant has exceeded its applicable leak rate. Unless an automatic leak detection system is used, what leak inspection schedule does 40 CFR 82.157 set for it?

options.A: Once every three months
options.B: Once every five years
options.C: Once per calendar year
options.D: Once every two years

questions.explanation: For comfort cooling appliances, leak inspections "must be conducted once per calendar year" until the owner shows the appliance has not leaked above the applicable rate for one year. Inspections every three months apply to commercial and industrial process refrigeration appliances of 500 pounds or more.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of a chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant chooses to retire it instead of repairing leaks. What is the longest schedule the retrofit or retirement plan may set for completing the work?

options.A: Six months
options.B: One year
options.C: Three years
options.D: Two years

questions.explanation: A retrofit or retirement plan must include "A schedule, not to exceed one-year" for completing the work. More time is possible only through the specific extensions the rule describes, not as a default plan schedule.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An appliance with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant must be reported to EPA as chronically leaking if it leaks what share of its full charge in a calendar year?

options.A: 35 percent or more
options.B: 50 percent or more
options.C: 100 percent or more
options.D: 125 percent or more

questions.explanation: Owners of appliances that "leak 125 percent or more of the full charge in a calendar year" must report to EPA. The report is due by March 1 of the following year and must describe efforts to find and repair the leaks.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For an appliance with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant, purged refrigerant is left out of the annual leak rate only if it is destroyed at what verifiable destruction efficiency?

options.A: 98 percent or greater
options.B: 90 percent or greater
options.C: 80 percent or greater
options.D: 75 percent or greater

questions.explanation: Purged refrigerant "destroyed at a verifiable destruction efficiency of 98 percent or greater" is not counted toward the leak rate (paragraph (k)). Owners who use this exclusion must also keep monitoring records (paragraph (l)(9)) and notify EPA within 60 days after the facility first uses it (paragraph (m)(5)).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under §82.158(d), if recovery or recycling equipment certified by an approved equipment testing organization has a noncondensables purge device, what is the most refrigerant it may release through purging?

options.A: 1 percent of the refrigerant being recycled
options.B: 3 percent of the refrigerant being recycled
options.C: 5 percent of the refrigerant being recycled
options.D: 10 percent of the refrigerant being recycled

questions.explanation: The equipment standard says such equipment "must not release more than 3 percent" of the refrigerant being recycled through noncondensables purging. This is measured under the conditions of the applicable test appendix (B1, B2, B3, or B4).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.158, Standards for recovery and/or recycling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A technician needs to open only one part of a low-pressure chiller. When may the technician evacuate just that part instead of the entire appliance?

options.A: When the opening is smaller than 4 square inches of flow area
options.B: When the job will take less than 15 minutes
options.C: When the refrigerant in the part can be isolated to a system receiver
options.D: When the chiller holds less than 50 pounds of refrigerant

questions.explanation: Technicians may evacuate "either the entire appliance or the part to be serviced, if the refrigerant in the part can be isolated to a system receiver." The 4-square-inch and 15-minute figures come from the definition of a major repair, not from this permission.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Before opening a low-pressure appliance (when none of the rule's exceptions apply), what must the technician evacuate to the Table 1 level?

options.A: The refrigerant, including all the liquid refrigerant
options.B: Only the refrigerant vapor
options.C: Only the refrigerant held in the compressor
options.D: Only the refrigerant held in the purge unit

questions.explanation: Technicians "must evacuate the refrigerant, including all the liquid refrigerant, to the levels in Table 1" using certified recovery and/or recycling equipment. Removing only the vapor, or only one component's refrigerant, leaves liquid behind and does not meet the rule.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A low-pressure chiller has a full charge of 400 pounds of refrigerant. Under what condition may system-dependent recovery equipment be used on it?

options.A: When a certified Type III technician supervises the recovery
options.B: When the recovery equipment was made before November 15, 1993
options.C: When the refrigerant will be returned to the same chiller
options.D: When the system-dependent equipment is permanently attached to the chiller as a pump-out unit

questions.explanation: System-dependent equipment "may not be used with appliances with a full charge of more than 15 pounds of refrigerant, unless the system-dependent equipment is permanently attached to the appliance as a pump-out unit." Supervision, equipment age, and where the refrigerant goes do not lift this limit.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Who is exempt from the requirement to use certified, self-contained recovery and/or recycling equipment?

options.A: Any certified Type III technician working on chillers
options.B: Persons who maintain, service, repair, or dispose of only appliances that they own and that contain pump-out units
options.C: Contractors servicing appliances with a full charge of less than 200 pounds
options.D: Anyone recovering R-123

questions.explanation: The exemption covers persons who work on "only appliances that they own and that contain pump-out units." Being a Type III technician, the charge size, or the refrigerant used does not create an exemption.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A low-pressure chiller must be evacuated to the Table 1 level before it is disposed of. Which activity does the definition of disposal include?

options.A: Disassembling the chiller for reuse of its component parts
options.B: Replacing a filter on its purge unit
options.C: Adding refrigerant to it
options.D: Measuring its pressures with gauges

questions.explanation: Disposal means the process leading to and including several activities, one of which is "The disassembly of any appliance for reuse of its component parts." Routine filter changes, charging or pressure readings are service work, not disposal.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A technician performs a follow-up verification test on a repaired leak in a chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant. What must the technician do when the service is finished?

options.A: Send the test results to EPA within 30 days
options.B: Give the owner or operator documentation of the test that meets the recordkeeping requirements
options.C: Keep the only copy of the results at the technician's place of business
options.D: Nothing; verification test records are the owner's job alone

questions.explanation: Technicians conducting initial or follow-up verification tests "must, upon conclusion of that service, provide the owner or operator of the appliance with documentation that meets these requirements" (location, dates, repaired leaks tested, test types, and results). The rule does not call for sending the results to EPA.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An industrial process refrigeration chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant is leaking above its applicable rate when refrigerant is added. The repair requires an industrial process shutdown. Without any extension, how long does the owner have to identify and repair the leaks?

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 180 days
options.C: 120 days
options.D: 270 days

questions.explanation: Leaks must be identified and repaired "within 30 days (or 120 days if an industrial process shutdown is required)." Because a shutdown is required, the 120-day period applies; 180 and 270 days are only outer limits of the extension for unavailable parts.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An industrial process refrigeration appliance with a full charge of 800 pounds of a class II refrigerant has exceeded its applicable leak rate. With no automatic leak detection system, how often must leak inspections be conducted?

options.A: Once every three months, until the leak rate calculations show four quarters in a row without exceeding the leak rate
options.B: Once per calendar year, until the leak rate calculations show one year without exceeding the leak rate
options.C: Once every two years, until the leak rate calculations show one year without exceeding the leak rate
options.D: Only once, right after the repair

questions.explanation: For commercial and industrial process refrigeration appliances with "a full charge of 500 or more pounds, leak inspections must be conducted once every three months" until four quarters in a row stay within the leak rate. Once per calendar year applies to those of 50 to under 500 pounds and to comfort cooling.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the federal definition, what does it mean to mothball an appliance?

options.A: Convert it from one refrigerant to another
options.B: Remove the refrigerant and disable the refrigerant circuit so no one can use it again
options.C: Keep it running with a reduced refrigerant charge
options.D: Evacuate the refrigerant to at least atmospheric pressure and temporarily shut it down

questions.explanation: Mothball means to evacuate refrigerant "to at least atmospheric pressure, and to temporarily shut down that appliance." Making the appliance permanently unusable is the definition of retire, and converting refrigerants is retrofit.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of a chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant mothballs it while a leak repair deadline is running. When does the repair time frame resume?

options.A: On the day EPA approves the mothballing
options.B: On the day additional refrigerant is added to the appliance
options.C: 30 days after the appliance is mothballed
options.D: On January 1 of the following year

questions.explanation: The repair time frames "are temporarily suspended when an appliance is mothballed", and "The time will resume on the day additional refrigerant is added to the appliance." The rule does not tie the restart to EPA approval or a fixed number of days.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For an appliance with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant, when must the owner or operator calculate the leak rate?

options.A: Once per calendar year
options.B: Only during a leak inspection
options.C: Every time refrigerant is added, unless the addition follows a retrofit or installation of a new appliance, or qualifies as a seasonal variance
options.D: Only when the appliance is retired

questions.explanation: The owner or operator "must calculate the leak rate every time refrigerant is added to an appliance", except right after a retrofit, at installation of a new appliance, or for a seasonal variance. A yearly calculation would miss additions in between.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A facility has several chillers subject to the leak repair requirements. What does the leak rate definition require about the calculation method?

options.A: The same method must be used for all appliances subject to the leak repair requirements at the facility
options.B: Each appliance must use a different method
options.C: The technician may switch methods at each refrigerant addition
options.D: Comfort cooling appliances must use one method and industrial process refrigeration another

questions.explanation: The definition states: "The same method must be used for all appliances subject to the leak repair requirements located at an operating facility." Switching methods between appliances or between additions is not allowed.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the federal definition, how is an appliance's leak rate expressed?

options.A: As pounds of refrigerant lost per month
options.B: As the percentage of the full charge lost since the appliance was installed
options.C: As the percentage of the full charge lost over the last 30 days
options.D: As the percentage of the full charge that would be lost over a 12-month period if the current rate of loss continued

questions.explanation: The leak rate is "the percentage of the appliance's full charge that would be lost over a 12-month period if the current rate of loss were to continue over that period." It is a percentage of full charge projected over 12 months, not pounds or a loss since installation.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: On an appliance with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant, leaks were repaired. Which situation lets the leaks be presumed repaired?

options.A: The owner signs a statement that the repair is complete
options.B: No further refrigerant is added for 12 months after the repair
options.C: The appliance runs for 30 days without shutting down
options.D: A technician adds a full charge of refrigerant

questions.explanation: The leaks "will be presumed to be repaired if there is no further refrigerant addition for 12 months after the repair" or if the required leak inspections find no leaks. A signed statement or a period of operation is not named as a basis.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: On a comfort cooling chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant (no industrial process shutdown), replacement components are not available within 30 days. Under the extension for unavailable components, how much time is permitted?

options.A: Up to 30 days after delivery, but not more than 270 days from the date the appliance exceeded the leak rate
options.B: Up to one year after the components are ordered
options.C: Up to 30 days after delivery, but not more than 180 days from the date the appliance exceeded the leak rate
options.D: As long as needed, with no limit

questions.explanation: Additional time is permitted "up to 30 days after receiving delivery of the necessary components, not to exceed 180 days" from the date the appliance exceeded the leak rate. The 270-day limit applies only when an industrial process shutdown is required.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of a chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant requests more time for leak repairs under §82.157(f). How is the request treated?

options.A: It is considered approved unless EPA notifies the owner or operator otherwise
options.B: It takes effect only after EPA sends written approval
options.C: It must first be approved at a public hearing
options.D: It is available only to federally owned appliances

questions.explanation: For repair deadline extensions, "The request will be considered approved unless EPA notifies the owners or operators otherwise." No written approval or hearing is needed, and the extension is not limited to federal equipment.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant leaks above its applicable rate, and the owner intends to retire it rather than repair the leak. By when must a retrofit or retirement plan be created?

options.A: Within one year of the leak
options.B: Within seven months of discovering the leak
options.C: By March 1 of the following year
options.D: Within 30 days of the appliance leaking above the applicable leak rate

questions.explanation: The owner or operator "must create a retrofit or retirement plan within 30 days of" the appliance leaking above the applicable rate when it intends to retrofit or retire rather than repair. Seven months is the deadline for asking EPA for more than one year to finish the work, not for creating the plan.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For an appliance with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant, which requirement applies to a retrofit or retirement plan?

options.A: It must be filed with the state environmental agency
options.B: It must be signed by an authorized company official, dated, and accessible at the site of the appliance
options.C: It must be signed by a Type III technician and mailed to the appliance manufacturer
options.D: It must be posted publicly online

questions.explanation: The plan "must be signed by an authorized company official, dated, accessible at the site of the appliance" in paper or electronic form and available for EPA inspection on request. The rule does not call for a technician's signature, state filing, or public posting.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of a comfort cooling chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant will retire it and replace it with an appliance using a substitute refrigerant exempted under §82.154(a). How long is the owner automatically allowed to retire the chiller?

options.A: One year
options.B: 13 months
options.C: 18 months
options.D: 30 weeks

questions.explanation: Owners or operators "are automatically allowed 18 months to retire an appliance if the replacement appliance uses a substitute refrigerant exempted under § 82.154(a)." One year (and at most 13 months) is the normal limit when this extension does not apply.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For an appliance with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant, which item must the leak inspection records include?

options.A: A certification that all visible and accessible parts of the appliance were inspected
options.B: A photograph of each leak
options.C: The signature of an EPA inspector
options.D: The technician's Social Security number

questions.explanation: Leak inspection records must include the date, the method(s) used, the location of each leak found, and "a certification that all visible and accessible parts of the appliance were inspected." Photographs, an EPA signature, or a Social Security number are not listed.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of a chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant will retrofit it to a different refrigerant under a retrofit or retirement plan. What must happen to the leaks that have been identified?

options.A: They may be left as they are, because the refrigerant is being changed
options.B: Only leaks larger than the applicable leak rate must be repaired
options.C: They must be reported to EPA instead of repaired
options.D: All identified leaks must be repaired as part of the retrofit

questions.explanation: The rule states: "All identified leaks must be repaired as part of any retrofit under such a plan." Changing the refrigerant does not remove the duty to fix the leaks found.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of a comfort cooling chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant uses a repair deadline extension because one part is on back order. Other leaks that significantly contribute to the leak rate can be fixed without extra time. When must those repairs be completed and verified?

options.A: Within 30 days of receiving the back-ordered part
options.B: Within the initial 30-day repair period
options.C: Within 180 days of the appliance exceeding the leak rate
options.D: Before the next annual leak inspection

questions.explanation: Repairs to leaks that significantly contribute to the exceedance "and that do not require additional time must be completed and verified within the initial 30 day repair period" (120 days if an industrial process shutdown is required). The extra time covers only the repair that needs the missing part.

questions.question: Before a closed-book Type III test, how must proctors verify the identity of the people taking it?

options.A: By asking for their Social Security number
options.B: By checking a recent utility bill
options.C: By examining photo identification
options.D: No identity check is required

questions.explanation: Appendix D states: "Proctors are required to verify the identity of individuals taking the test by examining photo identification." Accepted forms include drivers' licenses, government identification cards, passports and military identification.
